page: Amazon Web Services x8i.metal-48xl is a bare-metal, memory-optimized compute instance designed for extreme in-memory footprints and parallel processing. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it features a dedicated 96-core Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor operating at 3.9 GHz, delivering 192 virtual execution threads via symmetric multithreading. The processor incorporates 480 MB of shared L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel AMX for matrix multiplication. Memory configuration comprises 3072 GB of high-speed 7 GHz DDR5 RAM, equating to 16 GB per virtual core. Baseline network throughput reaches 75 Gbps, while dedicated hardware virtualization ensures direct hardware access without hypervisor overhead.

Benchmark evaluations reveal exceptional multi-core throughput and memory subsystem capacity. In multi-threaded computational workloads, the instance achieves top-tier results, generating a stress-ng multi-core score of 209,138.43, a PassMark CPU score of 145,068.25, and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 1197.68 GB/sec. Large block uncached memory read bandwidth exceeds 525 GB/sec, driving top-tier database performance of 34,880.31 operations in PassMark testing and over 271 million Redis SET operations per second. Prompt processing for large language models, including 70B parameter models, also demonstrates top-decile throughput due to extensive memory channels and AMX support, while single-core execution metrics across stress-ng and Geekbench sit in the average to upper-quartile ranges.

The primary architectural tradeoff of the x8i.metal-48xl lies in its storage and accelerator configurations. The instance includes no bundled local NVMe storage and contains zero GPUs, necessitating reliance on network-attached storage architectures and CPU-based instruction paths for inferencing tasks. From a resource perspective, the instance provides qualitative cost efficiency for monolithic in-memory architectures where multi-terabyte datasets must reside entirely within physical RAM. The massive thread density and DDR5 bandwidth avoid multi-node partitioning complexity, making it well matched for enterprise in-memory databases, large-scale Redis or Memcached clusters, memory-intensive ETL pipelines, and high-concurrency static web serving.
description: Amazon Web Services x8i.metal-48xl is a bare-metal memory-optimized instance featuring 96 physical cores and 192 vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor clocked at 3.9 GHz. Operating on x86_64 architecture with 480 MB of L3 cache, AVX-512, and AMX support, it provides 3072 GB of 7 GHz DDR5 memory alongside a 75 Gbps network interface. The instance includes no local storage or discrete GPUs, requiring external network storage. Benchmark evaluations highlight top-tier multi-threaded compute and memory throughput, demonstrated by over 271 million Redis SET operations per second, high uncached memory read bandwidth of 525.98 GB/sec, and strong large language model prompt evaluation. While single-core performance remains moderate, the hardware consolidation of massive memory density and bare-metal CPU parallelism makes the instance suited for large in-memory databases, real-time analytics, and high-concurrency data processing pipelines.
